podcast.title: Andy Wise's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Keyboardist and saxophonist Andy Wise transitioned to working as an electrician in Fort McMurray's oil sands, where he also played in a band called Backbone and sometimes led or judged karaoke sessions. He currently resides in Yorkton, Saskatchewan. "Andy Wise, the keyboardist and sacks guy, went on to work as an electrician in Fort McMurray in the oil sands where he played in a band called Backbone and occasionally led and judged karaoke sessions."

podcast.title: Bob McQuits' Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Bob McQuits pursued a career in sports radio after his time with Glüleg. This represents a complete transition from music into media. "Bob McQuits went on to a career in sports radio."

podcast.title: Carlos Alonzo's Continued Music Activity
podcast.body: Original singer and stick player Carlos Alonzo took a hiatus from music but spent part of 2018 recording an album at Peter Gabriel's prestigious Real World Studios in Newland. This signifies a high-profile return to recording. "original singer and stick player Carlos Alonzo was out of music for a while but spent part of 2018 recording an album at Peter Gabriel's real world studio's Newland."

podcast.title: Carlos Alonzo's Stick Instrument
podcast.body: Singer Carlos Alonzo utilized an instrument known as a "stick," a long fretboard typically featuring 10 or 12 strings, which was considered challenging to play. This unique instrument was integral to Glüleg's distinct musical identity. "Carlos Alonzo played something called a stick, which is essentially one big long fretboard with either 10 or 12 strings, not the easiest thing to play."

podcast.title: Chowder's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Bass player "Chowder" later worked with Moist and David Usher. He now works at a BMW motorcycle shop and occasionally performs at quiet, anonymous gigs and open mics, indicating a partial return to music. "Chowder, the bass player, later worked with Moist and David Usher, now works at BMW in the motorcycle shop and still plays the odd time."

podcast.title: Christian Samson's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Drummer Christian Samson played with Edwin after his departure from I Mother Earth, had brief stints with Moist and the prog rock group Saga, and now manages his own HVAC condo service. This shows a diverse career path both within and outside the music industry. "drummer Christian Samson played around with Edwin after he left I Mother Earth. There was also a short stint in Moist and with saga, the Prague Rock Group, and he's now running his own HVAC condo service."

podcast.title: Origin and Genre Experimentation
podcast.body: Glüleg formed in Guelph, Ontario, before relocating to Toronto to explore a distinctive fusion of rock, jazz, funk, and possibly rap. Their sound was notably unique in Canada at the time, described as making "an awful lot of noise for just a few guys." "They were originally from Guelph, Ontario, but moved to Toronto to experiment with a mix of rock, jazz, funk, and something else. Rap, maybe?"

podcast.title: Ruben Huzenga's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Guitarist Ruben Huzenga now owns and operates his own studio, where he has collaborated with Edwin and Big Wreck. This indicates his continued engagement in music production and collaboration within the Canadian scene. "Guitarist Ruben Huzenga has his own studio where he's worked with Edwin and also with Big Rec."

podcast.title: Sylvia Massey Production
podcast.body: Glüleg's third album was produced by Sylvia Massey, a highly respected figure in music production with a resume that includes working with Tool, Red Hot Chili Peppers, System of a Down, and Cage the Elephant. Her involvement highlights the band's artistic credibility. "the third of which was produced by Sylvia Massey, a woman who has everyone from tool to the Red Hot Chili Peppers, to system of a down to cage the elephant on her resume."

xref.body: Edwin left I Mother Earth, subsequently engaging in collaborations with Christian Samson (drummer of Glüleg). His departure marked a significant lineup change for the band and allowed Edwin to pursue new musical ventures. "Christian Samson played around with Edwin after he left I Mother Earth."
